definitions.explanation: The force that propels an object forward, especially in the context of engines, rockets, and aircraft.

examples.japanese: エンジンの{推力|すいりょく}を{上|あ}げる。
このロケットは{大|おお}きな{推力|すいりょく}を{持|も}つ。
{新型|しんがた}エンジンは{従来|じゅうらい}より30パーセント{推力|すいりょく}が{向上|こうじょう}した。
examples.english: The new engine has 30 percent more thrust than the previous model.

notes:
Composed of {推|すい} (push forward) + {力|りょく} (force). A technical term used in aerospace, physics, and engineering. Commonly appears in news about rocket launches, aviation, and engine development.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {推力|すいりょく}を{発生|はっせい}させる: to generate thrust
- {最大|さいだい}{推力|すいりょく}: maximum thrust
- {推力|すいりょく}{不足|ふそく}: insufficient thrust
- {推力|すいりょく}{重量比|じゅうりょうひ}: thrust-to-weight ratio

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {推進力|すいしんりょく}: propulsion; driving force — can be used both literally (physical propulsion) and figuratively (driving force behind a project)
- {馬力|ばりき}: horsepower — a unit measuring engine power output, not directly the forward force
- {水力|すいりょく}: hydropower — a homophone with the same reading but different kanji ({水|すい} instead of {推|すい}), referring to the power of water
